newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rostock port falling behind in cocoa shipments.
newsitem.headline: Rostock port falling behind in cocoa shipments.

text.p: The Baltic Sea port of Rostock has failed to achieve higher cocoa handling goals envisaged in the early 1990s and in 1996 fell further behind its main competitor, Hamburg, the cocoa trade organisation VRBF said.
In 1996 Rostock handled a mere 1,026 tonnes of cocoa bean imports after 18,200 tonnes in 1995, while the second largest cocoa port, Bremen, also lost out to Hamburg, VRBF's annual report said.
Transit shipments via Rostock declined to nil in 1996 after 25 tonnes in 1995 and 3,900 tonnes in 1994, it showed.
Hamburg achieved record imports of 197,264 tonnes in 1996 (151,851 tonnes 1995) plus transit volumes of 27,556 tonnes (20,152 in 1995).
Hamburg especially increased transit volumes for onward shipment to Denmark, Finland and Slovakia, Italy, Poland and Switzerland.
Bremen cocoa bean imports in 1996 declined 11.8 percent to 31,828 and transit shipments of 8,168 tonnes, mainly to Slovakia and Austria, were 20.7 percent down from 1995.

After the collapse of communism Rostock hoped to become a major location for bean volumes aimed at Scandinavia and eastern Europe. Chocolate manufacturers in West Berlin would have been ideal customers but they closed plants after losing special tax breaks which had been in place up to 1989.
